-------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m5p2t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Floors, Elevators, Controllers, Quorum, HeadCount

VARIABLES waiting, riding, proposal, votes

vars == <<waiting, riding, proposal, votes>>

RECURSIVE SetSum(_, _)
SetSum(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SetSum(f, S \ {x})

PeopleCount == SetSum(waiting, Floors) + SetSum(riding, Elevators)

NoProposal == [kind |-> "none", floor |-> "", car |-> ""]

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \in [Floors -> 0..HeadCount]
    /\ riding \in [Elevators -> 0..HeadCount]
    /\ proposal \in [kind : {"none", "board", "exit"},
                     floor : Floors \cup {""}, car : Elevators \cup {""}]
    /\ votes \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ waiting = [f \in Floors |-> IF f = CHOOSE g \in Floors : TRUE
                                   THEN HeadCount ELSE 0]
    /\ riding = [e \in Elevators |-> 0]
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ votes = {}

ProposeBoard ==
    /\ proposal.kind = "none"
    /\ \E f \in Floors, e \in Elevators :
         /\ waiting[f] > 0
         /\ proposal' = [kind |-> "board", floor |-> f, car |-> e]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, riding>>

ProposeExit ==
    /\ proposal.kind = "none"
    /\ \E f \in Floors, e \in Elevators :
         /\ riding[e] > 0
         /\ proposal' = [kind |-> "exit", floor |-> f, car |-> e]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, riding>>

CastVote ==
    /\ proposal.kind # "none"
    /\ \E c \in Controllers :
         /\ c \notin votes
         /\ votes' = votes \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, riding, proposal>>

Commit ==
    /\ proposal.kind # "none"
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ LET f == proposal.floor
           e == proposal.car
       IN IF proposal.kind = "board"
          THEN /\ waiting[f] > 0
               /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
               /\ riding'  = [riding  EXCEPT ![e] = @ + 1]
          ELSE /\ riding[e] > 0
               /\ riding'  = [riding  EXCEPT ![e] = @ - 1]
               /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ votes' = {}

Next == ProposeBoard \/ ProposeExit \/ CastVote \/ Commit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PopulationConserved == PeopleCount = HeadCount
=============================================================================
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper moves a fixed group of people between two floors and a single shared car. People are only ever waiting on a floor or riding in the car; the bank never conjures a new person and never loses one. Every physical move of people must first be approved by a quorum of the building's independent safety controllers rather than by a single controller. A move begins when one proposal (board the car from a floor, or exit the car to a floor) is put forward while no other proposal is outstanding. Each controller then casts its vote for the outstanding proposal; because the controllers sit on a lossy bus, their votes may arrive in any order and are simply accumulated. Once at least a quorum of controllers have voted, the proposed move is committed atomically: the people are removed from the source and added to the destination, and the proposal slot is cleared for the next one. Because a commit only ever relocates people and never mints or drops them, the head count of the whole bank stays fixed forever.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of people summed across every floor and the car always equals the fixed head count the bank started with.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m4p5t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patients, NumRooms, MinCap, MaxCap

VARIABLES inQueue, inRoom, operated, capacity

vars == <<inQueue, inRoom, operated, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ inQueue \subseteq Patients
    /\ inRoom \subseteq Patients
    /\ operated \subseteq Patients
    /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap

Idle(p) == p \notin inQueue /\ p \notin inRoom /\ p \notin operated

Init ==
    /\ inQueue = {}
    /\ inRoom = {}
    /\ operated = {}
    /\ capacity = MinCap

Enqueue ==
    /\ \E p \in Patients :
         /\ Idle(p)
         /\ Cardinality(inQueue) < capacity
         /\ inQueue' = inQueue \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inRoom, operated, capacity>>

Admit ==
    /\ \E p \in inQueue :
         /\ p \notin operated
         /\ Cardinality(inRoom) < NumRooms
         /\ inQueue' = inQueue \ {p}
         /\ inRoom' = inRoom \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<operated, capacity>>

Operate ==
    /\ \E p \in inRoom :
         /\ p \notin operated
         /\ inRoom' = inRoom \ {p}
         /\ operated' = operated \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inQueue, capacity>>

RaiseCapacity ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inQueue, inRoom, operated>>

LowerCapacity ==
    /\ capacity > MinCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inQueue, inRoom, operated>>

Next == Enqueue \/ Admit \/ Operate \/ RaiseCapacity \/ LowerCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OperatedNeverInPipeline ==
    (inQueue \cup inRoom) \cap operated = {}
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Patients = {p1, p2, p3}
    NumRooms = 1
    MinCap = 1
    MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OperatedNeverInPipeline
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler moves patients through a bounded admission queue toward surgery. A patient starts uncommitted, is enqueued for surgery, is admitted into a free operating room, and is finally operated on. The admission queue applies backpressure: a patient may only be enqueued while the number already waiting in the queue is strictly below the current capacity limit. Operating rooms are also limited, so a queued patient can only be admitted while a room is free. The act of operating is irreversible and must happen at most once per patient: once a patient has been operated on, that patient must never be pushed back into the queue or into a room again. The scheduler may also change the queue capacity at runtime, raising it when staff arrive and lowering it when staff leave, but never below one. Because every enqueue and admit step refuses any patient who has already been operated on, an operated patient can never reappear anywhere in the live pipeline. Thus no patient is ever operated on twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No patient who has already been operated on is ever simultaneously waiting in the queue or occupying an operating room.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m1p1t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Jobs, Slots, NULL, NONE

VARIABLES holder, traveling, record, written, acked

vars == <<holder, traveling, record, written, acked>>

Contents == { record[s] : s \in Slots } \ {NULL}

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ traveling \in BOOLEAN
    /\ record \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {NULL}]
    /\ written \subseteq Jobs
    /\ acked \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
    /\ holder = NONE
    /\ traveling = TRUE
    /\ record = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]
    /\ written = {}
    /\ acked = {}

AcquireToken ==
    /\ traveling = TRUE
    /\ holder = NONE
    /\ \E n \in Nodes : holder' = n
    /\ traveling' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, written, acked>>

ReleaseToken ==
    /\ holder # NONE
    /\ holder' = NONE
    /\ traveling' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, written, acked>>

WriteJob ==
    /\ holder # NONE
    /\ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots :
         /\ j \notin written
         /\ record[s] = NULL
         /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![s] = j]
         /\ written' = written \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, traveling, acked>>

AckJob ==
    /\ \E j \in written :
         /\ j \notin acked
         /\ acked' = acked \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, traveling, record, written>>

Next == AcquireToken \/ ReleaseToken \/ WriteJob \/ AckJob

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == written = Contents
=============================================================================
nl:
A print shop spooler lets several workstations write jobs into a small shared spool that has a fixed set of named slots. To prevent two workstations from clobbering each other's writes, a single token grants exclusive write access, and only the workstation currently holding the token may place a job. The token travels on a lossy internal bus rather than a strict ring, so token grants can be delivered out of order and any idle workstation may end up picking up the free token next. A workstation may only drop a not-yet-recorded job into a slot that is currently empty, so a job that is already recorded in the spool is never overwritten by a later write. After a job is spooled it may later be acknowledged. Because writes only ever fill empty slots under the protection of the single token, no previously recorded job can be lost. Thus the set of jobs the shop believes it recorded always matches exactly the jobs physically present in the spool slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job that has been recorded as written is still physically present in some spool slot, and no recorded job has been overwritten.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m3p0t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Controllers, Runways, Aircraft, FREE, NONE

VARIABLES leader, alive, lease, occupant, onRunway

vars == <<leader, alive, lease, occupant, onRunway>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in [Instances -> Controllers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ alive \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ lease \in [Runways -> Instances \cup {FREE}]
    /\ occupant \in [Runways -> Aircraft \cup {NONE}]
    /\ onRunway \in [Aircraft -> Runways \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ leader = [i \in Instances |-> NONE]
    /\ alive = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]
    /\ lease = [r \in Runways |-> FREE]
    /\ occupant = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]
    /\ onRunway = [a \in Aircraft |-> NONE]

LeadsSomewhere(c) == \E i \in Instances : leader[i] = c

Elect ==
    /\ \E i \in Instances, c \in Controllers :
         /\ leader[i] = NONE
         /\ alive[c]
         /\ ~LeadsSomewhere(c)
         /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, lease, occupant, onRunway>>

FailLeader ==
    /\ \E i \in Instances :
         /\ leader[i] # NONE
         /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader[i]] = FALSE]
         /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, occupant, onRunway>>

Grant ==
    /\ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways, a \in Aircraft :
         /\ leader[i] # NONE
         /\ lease[r] = FREE
         /\ onRunway[a] = NONE
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r] = i]
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![r] = a]
         /\ onRunway' = [onRunway EXCEPT ![a] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Release ==
    /\ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways :
         /\ leader[i] # NONE
         /\ lease[r] = i
         /\ occupant[r] # NONE
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r] = FREE]
         /\ onRunway' = [onRunway EXCEPT ![occupant[r]] = NONE]
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Recover ==
    /\ \E c \in Controllers :
         /\ ~alive[c]
         /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, lease, occupant, onRunway>>

Next == Elect \/ FailLeader \/ Grant \/ Release \/ Recover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ExclusiveLanding ==
    \A a \in Aircraft : onRunway[a] # NONE => occupant[onRunway[a]] = a
=============================================================================
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator coordinates landings over a shared pool of runways. Two independent allocator instances, one per approach sector, draw from the very same pool of physical runways, so they must never both put an aircraft onto the same runway. Within each instance a leader controller is elected from a set of controllers, and only a live elected leader may grant a runway. Leaders can fail: a live leader may crash, which clears that instance's leadership until a new controller is elected to take over. A leader grants a runway to an aircraft only when that runway is free of any lease, recording both that the runway now holds the aircraft and that the aircraft is now on that runway. When landing finishes, the leader releases the runway, freeing its lease and clearing both records. A crashed controller may later recover and become available for election again. The allocator keeps two coupled views: for each runway who occupies it, and for each aircraft which runway it sits on. Because a grant only ever touches a lease-free runway, these two views can never disagree. Therefore no aircraft is ever recorded on a runway that some other aircraft simultaneously occupies.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every aircraft that believes it is on a runway, that runway records exactly that aircraft as its occupant, so no two aircraft ever share a runway.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m4p0t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Locks, Agents, MinCap, MaxCap, NONE

VARIABLES waiting, occupant, holds, capacity

vars == <<waiting, occupant, holds, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \in [Locks -> SUBSET Agents]
    /\ occupant \in [Locks -> Agents \cup {NONE}]
    /\ holds \in [Agents -> Locks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ waiting = [l \in Locks |-> {}]
    /\ occupant = [l \in Locks |-> NONE]
    /\ holds = [a \in Agents |-> NONE]
    /\ capacity = MinCap

Request ==
    /\ \E l \in Locks, a \in Agents :
         /\ a \notin waiting[l]
         /\ occupant[l] # a
         /\ Cardinality(waiting[l]) < capacity
         /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![l] = @ \cup {a}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, holds, capacity>>

Enter ==
    /\ \E l \in Locks, a \in Agents :
         /\ a \in waiting[l]
         /\ occupant[l] = NONE
         /\ holds[a] = NONE
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![l] = a]
         /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![a] = l]
         /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![l] = @ \ {a}]
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Exit ==
    /\ \E l \in Locks, a \in Agents :
         /\ occupant[l] = a
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![l] = NONE]
         /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![a] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, capacity>>

RaiseCapacity ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, occupant, holds>>

LowerCapacity ==
    /\ capacity > MinCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, occupant, holds>>

Next == Request \/ Enter \/ Exit \/ RaiseCapacity \/ LowerCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion ==
    \A a \in Agents : holds[a] # NONE => occupant[holds[a]] = a
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Locks = {d1, d2}
    Agents = {u1, u2}
    MinCap = 1
    MaxCap = 2
    NONE = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network lets several household agents actuate a set of shared door locks. Each physical lock is a critical resource: at any instant at most one agent may be inside the actuation critical section of a given lock, because concurrent actuation would strip the motor. Agents that want a lock join that lock's bounded waiting queue, and backpressure means an agent may only join while that queue holds strictly fewer waiters than the current capacity limit. From the queue an agent may enter the critical section only when the lock is currently unheld. On exit the agent leaves the critical section and the lock becomes free again. The hub may change the queue capacity at runtime, raising it during busy mornings and lowering it at night, but never below one. The network tracks two coupled views: for each lock which agent, if any, currently holds it, and for each agent which lock, if any, it is currently holding. Because an agent only enters an unheld lock, these two views always agree. Therefore no lock is ever held by two agents at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every agent that is holding a lock, that lock records exactly that agent as its holder, so no lock is ever in the critical section of two agents simultaneously.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m5p5t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Sensors, Quorum

VARIABLES stage, votes, sealLedger, adminEnabled

vars == <<stage, votes, sealLedger, adminEnabled>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ stage \in [Cars -> {"queued", "washing", "done"}]
    /\ votes \in [Cars -> SUBSET Sensors]
    /\ sealLedger \subseteq Cars
    /\ adminEnabled \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ stage = [c \in Cars |-> "queued"]
    /\ votes = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
    /\ sealLedger = {}
    /\ adminEnabled = FALSE

Wash ==
    /\ \E c \in Cars :
         /\ stage[c] = "queued"
         /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "washing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, sealLedger, adminEnabled>>

CastVote ==
    /\ \E c \in Cars, s \in Sensors :
         /\ stage[c] = "washing"
         /\ s \notin votes[c]
         /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, sealLedger, adminEnabled>>

QuorumSeal ==
    /\ \E c \in Cars :
         /\ stage[c] = "washing"
         /\ Cardinality(votes[c]) >= Quorum
         /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
         /\ sealLedger' = sealLedger \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, adminEnabled>>

AdminSeal ==
    /\ adminEnabled
    /\ \E c \in Cars :
         /\ stage[c] = "washing"
         /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
         /\ sealLedger' = sealLedger \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, adminEnabled>>

ToggleAdmin ==
    /\ adminEnabled' = ~adminEnabled
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, votes, sealLedger>>

Next == Wash \/ CastVote \/ QuorumSeal \/ AdminSeal \/ ToggleAdmin

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SealedIffDone ==
    \A c \in Cars : (c \in sealLedger) <=> (stage[c] = "done")
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2}
    Sensors = {s1, s2, s3}
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SealedIffDone
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line moves cars through wash and then a final protective wax seal. Each car begins queued, is washed, and is finally sealed; the sealing step lays down a permanent wax coat and is irreversible, so any given car must be sealed at most once. Sealing a car normally requires a quorum of the line's independent quality sensors to vote in favor, since a bad seal ruins the finish. Sensors cast votes for a car over time and the votes accumulate until a quorum is reached, at which point the car may be sealed: it moves to the done stage and its identifier is written into the permanent seal ledger. A privileged plant administrator may also force a seal on a washed car, bypassing the sensor quorum entirely, for cars stuck behind flaky sensors. Whether the seal came from a quorum or from the admin override, it still only ever applies to a car that is currently washing and then marks it done, so a car already sealed can never be sealed again. The line keeps the seal ledger and the per-car stage exactly in lockstep.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A car appears in the permanent seal ledger if and only if its stage is done, so no car is ever sealed a second time.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m2p6t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants

VARIABLES phase, votesYes, authorized, synced

vars == <<phase, votesYes, authorized, synced>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "committed"}
    /\ votesYes \subseteq Participants
    /\ authorized \subseteq Participants
    /\ synced \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votesYes = {}
    /\ authorized = Participants
    /\ synced = [p \in Participants |-> TRUE]

StartRound ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votesYes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, synced>>

Sync ==
    /\ \E p \in Participants :
         /\ ~synced[p]
         /\ synced' = [synced EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votesYes, authorized>>

Vote ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E p \in Participants :
         /\ p \in authorized
         /\ synced[p]
         /\ p \notin votesYes
         /\ votesYes' = votesYes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, authorized, synced>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ authorized # {}
    /\ authorized \subseteq votesYes
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votesYes, authorized, synced>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E p \in Participants :
         /\ authorized' = IF p \in authorized THEN authorized \ {p}
                          ELSE authorized \cup {p}
         /\ synced' = [synced EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ votesYes' = {}

Reset ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ votesYes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, synced>>

Next == StartRound \/ Sync \/ Vote \/ Commit \/ Reconfigure \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyFreshAuthorizedVotes ==
    \A p \in votesYes : p \in authorized /\ synced[p]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyFreshAuthorizedVotes
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line commits a batch of bays to a wash cycle using a two-phase commit run by a coordinator. Each bay participant carries a synchronized flag saying whether it currently matches the coordinator's configuration. A round begins when the coordinator opens voting. Each bay that is currently authorized and synchronized may cast a yes vote, and votes accumulate; a bay only votes once per round. When every authorized bay has voted yes, the coordinator commits the batch. The line's capacity changes at runtime: an administrator may bring a bay online or take one offline, and any such reconfiguration also marks the touched bay as no longer synchronized and restarts the round with a cleared vote set, so bays that have not re-synchronized are stale. A stale bay may resynchronize at any time to set its flag back to synchronized. The crucial guarantee is that neither a stale bay nor a bay that is not currently authorized can ever have its vote counted. After a commit the coordinator returns to idle for the next round.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bay whose yes vote is currently counted is both authorized and synchronized.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m9p3t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Players, Slots, MaxEpoch, NONE

VARIABLES holder, occupies, epoch, crashed

vars == <<holder, occupies, epoch, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ occupies \in [Players -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ crashed \subseteq Players

Init ==
    /\ holder = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ occupies = [p \in Players |-> NONE]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

Allocate ==
    /\ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots :
         /\ p \notin crashed
         /\ occupies[p] = NONE
         /\ holder[s] = NONE
         /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = p]
         /\ occupies' = [occupies EXCEPT ![p] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

Release ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
         /\ holder[s] # NONE
         /\ occupies' = [occupies EXCEPT ![holder[s]] = NONE]
         /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ \E p \in Players :
         /\ p \notin crashed
         /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, occupies, epoch>>

Recover ==
    /\ \E p \in Players :
         /\ p \in crashed
         /\ crashed' = crashed \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, occupies, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holder' = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ occupies' = [p \in Players |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Next == Allocate \/ Release \/ Crash \/ Recover \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A p \in Players : occupies[p] # NONE => holder[occupies[p]] = p
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {pa, pb, pc}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NONE = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into a fixed set of match slots. Each slot may hold at most one player: the same slot must never be allocated to two players at once. The matchmaker keeps two coupled records, one saying for each slot which player occupies it, and one saying for each player which slot it occupies. A player is seated by allocating a currently empty slot, which writes both records together; leaving a slot clears both together. The lobby runs epoch-numbered reconfigurations: a reconfiguration bumps the lobby epoch and tears down all current seatings so the next match starts clean. Players can crash silently, simply dropping out without releasing their slot, in which case their seating lingers and continues to block that slot until the next reconfiguration; a crashed player may later reconnect. Because a slot is only ever allocated while empty and every allocation writes both coupled records, a player's record of its slot always matches that slot's record of its occupant. Therefore no slot is ever handed to two different players simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every player that occupies a slot, that slot records exactly that player as its occupant, so no slot is double-allocated.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m0p3t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Players, Slots, MaxVer, NONE

VARIABLES owner, claimSlot, version, attemptSlot, attemptVer, adminEnabled

vars == <<owner, claimSlot, version, attemptSlot, attemptVer, adminEnabled>>

Bump(v) == IF v < MaxVer THEN v + 1 ELSE v

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ claimSlot \in [Players -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ version \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ attemptSlot \in [Players -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ attemptVer \in [Players -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ adminEnabled \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ claimSlot = [p \in Players |-> NONE]
    /\ version = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ attemptSlot = [p \in Players |-> NONE]
    /\ attemptVer = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ adminEnabled = FALSE

ReadSlot ==
    /\ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots :
         /\ claimSlot[p] = NONE
         /\ attemptSlot[p] = NONE
         /\ attemptSlot' = [attemptSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]
         /\ attemptVer' = [attemptVer EXCEPT ![p] = version[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, claimSlot, version, adminEnabled>>

Commit ==
    /\ \E p \in Players :

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into match slots using optimistic locking with retry. Each slot has an occupant record and a version counter that ticks whenever the slot changes hands. To claim a slot a player first reads the slot's current version into a private attempt, then tries to commit: the commit succeeds only if the slot is still empty and its version is unchanged since the read, at which point the player becomes the occupant, the slot's version is bumped, and the player's own record of which slot it holds is written. A privileged administrator may also force-assign an empty slot to a player, bypassing the optimistic check entirely. Releasing a slot clears both the occupant and the player's record and bumps the version again. The matchmaker keeps the slot's occupant record and each player's held-slot record coupled. A bank's interbank settlement runs two independent settlement engines that share one common pool of ledger accounts. To keep the shared ledger consistent, writing an account is a critical section that only one engine node may enter at a time, coordinated by a single token that circulates on a ring. The token is either held by exactly one node or in transit on the bus between nodes; when in transit any node on the ring may pick it up next. A node may enter its write critical section only while it holds the token, and it must leave the critical section before it can pass the token onward. While inside the critical section a node settles an account, increasing that account's balance and recording itself as the account's last writer. Because there is only one token in the whole system and a node must hold it to enter, no two nodes from either engine can ever be settling at the same time. A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker finalizes matches drawn from one shared pool, served by two independent matchmaker instances. Finalizing a match writes its permanent result and is irreversible: a given match must be finalized at most once, even though both instances can reach into the same shared match pool. Within each instance a leader controller is elected from a set of controllers, and only a live elected leader may finalize a match. Leaders can fail: a live leader may crash, clearing that instance's leadership until a new controller is elected, and a crashed controller may later recover and stand for election again. When a live leader finalizes a still-open match, it does two things together: it stamps the match with a concrete result and it inscribes the match's identifier into the finalized registry. Because finalizing is only ever attempted on a match whose result is still empty, and the result stamp and the registry entry are always written as a pair, a match's result is present exactly when it appears in the registry. SAFETY PROPERTY: A match has a recorded result if and only if it appears in the finalized registry, so no match is finalized twice or half-finalized.

         /\ ~reading[w]
         /\ ~inCS[w]

         /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![w] = version]

         /\ lockHolder' = FREE
         /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVer, reading, crashed>>

         /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockHolder, version, inCS, readVer, reading>>

    MaxVer = 3

         /\ open' = open \ {b}
         /\ settled' = settled \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, votes, clock>>

         /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) < Quorum
         /\ open' = open \ {b}
         /\ pending' = pending \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, votes, clock>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, open, settled, votes>>

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch processes batches that move through three disjoint stages: pending, open, and settled. Settling a batch is irreversible and must happen at most once: a batch that has settled must never be settled again nor reappear as pending or open. A pending batch is first activated into the open stage where it can gather approvals. Settling requires a quorum of the consortium's validators to vote in favor of that batch. Validators can be slow, casting their votes late and in any order, but they never fail, so a quorum is always eventually reachable; votes for a batch simply accumulate. Once a batch has at least a quorum of votes, it may be settled, which moves it out of the open stage and into the settled stage in one step. A batch still in the open stage that has not gathered a quorum may be withdrawn back to pending. A shared settlement clock advances cyclically to mark the passage of time while slow validators catch up. Because a batch is settled only from the open stage and settling removes it from open, a settled batch is never simultaneously pending or open.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No settled batch is ever also present in the pending or open stage, so no batch is settled twice.

    /\ version \in [Zones -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ reading \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ readZone \in [Robots -> Zones \cup {NONE}]
    /\ readVer \in [Robots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ robotZone \in [Robots -> Zones \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ occupancy = [z \in Zones |-> 0]
    /\ version = [z \in Zones |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
    /\ readZone = [r \in Robots |-> NONE]
    /\ readVer = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ robotZone = [r \in Robots |-> NONE]

Read ==
    /\ \E r \in Robots, z \in Zones :
         /\ ~reading[r]
         /\ robotZone[r] = NONE
         /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
         /\ readZone' = [readZone EXCEPT ![r] = z]
         /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![r] = version[z]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, version, robotZone>>

CasEnter ==
    /\ \E r \in Robots :
         /\ reading[r]
         /\ readZone[r] # NONE
         /\ LET z == readZone[r] IN
              /\ version[z] = readVer[r]
              /\ occupancy[z] < Capacity
              /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![z] = @ + 1]
              /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![z] = Bump(@)]
              /\ robotZone' = [robotZone EXCEPT ![r] = z]
         /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readZone, readVer>>

CasFail ==
    /\ \E r \in Robots :
         /\ reading[r]
         /\ readZone[r] # NONE
         /\ LET z == readZone[r] IN
              version[z] # readVer[r] \/ occupancy[z] >= Capacity
         /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, version, readZone, readVer, robotZone>>

Leave ==
    /\ \E r \in Robots :
         /\ robotZone[r] # NONE
         /\ LET z == robotZone[r] IN
              /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![z] = @ - 1]
              /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![z] = Bump(@)]
         /\ robotZone' = [robotZone EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, readZone, readVer>>

Next == Read \/ CasEnter \/ CasFail \/ Leave

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A z \in Zones : occupancy[z] <= Capacity

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet routes robots into shared floor zones, where each zone may hold only up to a fixed capacity of robots at once. Each zone keeps an occupancy register counting how many robots are inside, together with a version counter, and robots contend for entry using optimistic locking with retry. Because entry requests are reordered on the fleet network, a robot first reads a chosen zone's occupancy and version into a private snapshot, then attempts a compare-and-swap: entry succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the read and the occupancy is still strictly below the zone's capacity, in which case the occupancy is incremented, the version is bumped, and the robot is recorded as being inside that zone. If the version moved or the zone is already full, the attempt fails and the robot retries from a fresh read. A robot that is inside a zone may leave, decrementing that zone's occupancy and bumping its version. Because entry only ever succeeds while a zone's occupancy is below capacity, and the compare-and-swap rejects any entry based on a stale read, no zone's occupancy can ever climb past its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every zone's occupancy count always stays at or below that zone's configured capacity.
